scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that development sometimes wins, then argues historic buildings deserve protection in most cases; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Cities must constantly decide whether to tear down the old or protect it.
Some people argue that when old buildings stand on useful ground, modern development should take precedence over preserving them.
I agree that development sometimes matters more, but I believe historic buildings deserve strong protection in most cases.
First, there are real cases where modern development should come first.
A growing city may badly need new homes, hospitals, or transport on valuable land.
For example, replacing a crumbling, empty building with housing can help many families in real need.
This shows that clinging to every old structure can block progress people genuinely require.
Not every old building is beautiful or historically important enough to save at any cost.
When human needs are urgent, sensible development can be the wiser choice.
To this extent, modern development sometimes deserves to take precedence.
Second, however, historic buildings usually deserve protection rather than destruction.
Old buildings carry the memory, beauty, and identity of a place across the generations.
Consider a historic town centre that draws visitors and gives its people a deep sense of belonging.
Such places show that once a historic building is lost, it can never truly be replaced.
Modern needs can often be met by building elsewhere or by restoring the old structure instead.
A society that destroys its past too easily loses something money can never buy back.
Preservation, then, should usually outweigh the simple convenience of new development.
In conclusion, modern development should sometimes take precedence when human needs are urgent.
But in most cases historic buildings deserve protection for their lasting value.
The wisest cities meet modern needs while carefully preserving the past that gives them meaning.
